Dans le cadre du Medicare Benefits Schedule, les médecins ne peuvent pas réclamer au gouvernement le paiement d’une vaccination contre la Covid-19 effectuée dans leur clinique par une infirmière, sauf si un médecin généraliste est présent sur place pour superviser.
To look over so as to read; to peruse.
(uncountable) The act or instance of supervising.
Under his parents' supervision he drilled the holes in the wood.
Sous la surveillance de ses parents, il a percé les trous dans le bois.
Do not attempt this without adequate supervision.
N’essayez pas cela sans une surveillance adéquate.
(management) A person with the official task of overseeing the work of a person or group, or of other operations and activities.

2001, Wendy Dobson, Gary Hufbauer, World Capital Markets, →ISBN, page…
La fusion de 1999 entre Citibank (banque) et Travelers (assurance) a créé le modèle de la méga-finance et confirmé de nouveaux défis pour les superviseurs.
A person who monitors someone to make sure they comply with rules or other requirements set for them.
A process responsible for managing other processes.
The clock burst which enables the supervisor to housekeep the console input and output and to change program status is currently set to 200 ms.
1965, P. A. Crisman, The compatible time-sharing system: a…
La rafale d’horloge qui permet au superviseur de gérer les entrées-sorties de la console et de modifier l’état du programme est actuellement réglée à 200 ms.
An optional light meal consumed shortly before going to bed.
Any meal eaten in the evening; dinner eaten in the evening, rather than at noon.
Food consumed before going to bed.
To provide (a person or animal) with supper.
However, once the calves have been suppered, the dogs must be fed too.
1984, John Barrington, “Glistening Glengyle”, in Red Sky at Night,…
Cependant, une fois les veaux nourris du souper, il faut aussi nourrir les chiens.
Something added; especially, such an addition added to make up for a deficiency.
AI models will not completely replace the humans, she said, but will serve as a “supplement” intended to aid in the brand’s representation of various sizes, skin tones and ages.

Les modèles d’IA ne remplaceront pas complètement les humains, a-t-elle déclaré, mais serviront de « complément » destiné à aider la marque à représenter des tailles, des teintes de peau et des âges variés.

A vitamin, herbal extract, or chemical compound ingested to meet dietary deficiencies or enhance muscular development; the dosage form that conveys or embodies it (e.g., tablet, capsule, pill, powder, beverage).
She wasn't getting enough iron, so they prescribed a supplement.
Elle ne consommait pas assez de fer, alors on lui a prescrit un complément.
A surcharge, additional cost, especially for food in a restaurant.
There is a £2 supplement if you choose the steak.
Il y a un supplément de 2 £ si vous choisissez le steak.
Someone who assists (sets up) a goal.
Regular supplier Barton played in another teasing corner, which was headed on towards goal by the impressive Ameobi and flicked in by expert poacher Nolan.
2011 January 16, Saj Chowdhury, “Sunderland 1 - 1 Newcastle”, in BBC
L’habituel fournisseur Barton a joué dans un autre coin plein de promesses, centré vers le but par l’impressionnant Ameobi, et redirigé au but par le renard des surfaces Nolan.
(transitive) To provide (something), to make (something) available for use.
to supply money for the war
fournir de l’argent pour la guerre
to supply a furnace with fuel; to supply soldiers with ammunition
alimenter une chaudière en combustible ; approvisionner des soldats en munitions
To fill up, or keep full.
Rivers are supplied by smaller streams.
Les rivières sont alimentées par de plus petits cours d’eau.
The company is responsible for the supply of electricity to the town.
L’entreprise est chargée de l’approvisionnement de la ville en électricité.
They are busy laying in supplies for the coming winter.
Ils sont occupés à faire des provisions pour l’hiver qui vient.
A supply of good drinking water is essential.
Un approvisionnement en eau potable de bonne qualité est essentiel.

The market force that causes sellers to be both willing and able to sell a good or service, as measured by the amount of that good or service that is currently available to be bought at any given price point; the amount itself.
Supply and demand ebb and flow in a complex interplay.
L’offre et la demande fluctuent dans une interaction complexe.
The chain of transportation mechanisms supplying food and materiel to an army in battle, or other field operation.
Having cracked the Germans' Enigma traffic, the Allies were able to devastate Rommel's supply lines across the Mediterranean.
Ayant percé les messages Enigma des Allemands, les Alliés purent anéantir les lignes de ravitaillement de Rommel en Méditerranée.
Don’t move that beam! It supports the whole platform.
Ne bouge pas cette poutre ! Elle soutient toute la plateforme.
To back or favor a cause, party, etc., mentally or with concrete aid
I support France in the World Cup.
Je soutiens la France à la Coupe du monde.
To provide sustenance or maintenance for; to sustain in integrity or livelihood.
Mars does not currently support human habitation.
Mars ne permet pas actuellement d’accueillir des humains.
Don't move that beam! It's a support for the whole platform.
Ne bouge pas cette poutre ! C’est un appui pour toute la plateforme.
The government provides support to the arts in several ways.
L’État soutient les arts de plusieurs façons.
Answers to questions and resolution of problems regarding something sold.
Sure they sell the product, but do they provide support?
Ils vendent le produit, d’accord, mais est-ce qu’ils assurent l’assistance ?
A group of people who informally support each other over a problem which all of its members share.
If you can't stay sober, you need a support group like Alcoholics Anonymous.
Si tu n’arrives pas à rester sobre, il te faut un groupe de soutien comme les Alcooliques anonymes.
A person who supports, promotes, advocates or champions a cause, movement, or political party; an adherent.
Linda Sanchez […] Strong supporter of intellectual property rights; consistently voted in favor of artists and songwriters on bills before the intellectual property subcommittee.
2006 November 4, Susan Butler, “Voters Guide: So Many Candidates.…

Linda Sanchez […] Fervente défenseuse des droits de propriété intellectuelle ; a constamment voté en faveur des artistes et des auteurs-compositeurs sur les projets de loi examinés par la sous-commission de la propriété intellectuelle.
(heraldry) An animal or figure that supports a shield in a coat of arms.
The lion and the unicorn are the supporters of the royal coat of arms.
Le lion et la licorne sont les tenants des armoiries royales.
A person who provides moral or physical support to another; an attendant participating in a ceremony or procession.
Her husband was her biggest supporter during her recovery.
Pendant sa convalescence, son mari a été son plus grand soutien.
Someone who is a fan of a certain sports team or sportsperson.
More than 10,000 supporters attended the last match.
Plus de 10 000 supporters ont assisté au dernier match.
I had a very supportive coach who helped me.
J’ai eu un entraîneur très bienveillant, qui m’a beaucoup aidé.
(transitive, intransitive) To take for granted; to conclude, with less than absolute supporting data; to believe.
I suppose we all agree that this is the best solution.
Je suppose que nous sommes tous d’accord pour dire que c’est la meilleure solution.
Suppose that A implies B and B implies C. Then A implies C.
Supposons que A implique B et que B implique C. Alors A implique C.
To imagine; to believe; to receive as true.
Je suppose que tu as raison.
To reckon to be, to account or esteem as.
As a matter of supposition; in the beliefs or according to the claims of some people.
People from other planets have supposedly visited Earth in flying saucers.
Des habitants d’autres planètes auraient visité la Terre à bord de soucoupes volantes.
Used in place of "supposed to be," often in informal or colloquial speech, as a mispronunciation.

D’après mes parents, je suis censé être au lit à 22 h.
To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.
La dissidence politique fut brutalement réprimée.
To restrain or repress, such as laughter or an expression.
I struggled to suppress my smile.
J’ai eu du mal à réprimer mon sourire.
To hold in place, to keep low.
An advocate of supremacism, a supporter of the belief that some groups should control others.
